= Development and Engineering Hygiene
:toc:

== Core principle

Hygiene is part of the feature.

Every change should leave the repository at least as understandable, testable, reproducible, and maintainable as it was before.

== Build hygiene

* The repository must build from a clean checkout.
* New warnings are not accepted.
* Build configuration must be reproducible.
* CI and local validation should use equivalent commands.
* Generated files must be separated from source files.

== Local validation

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs three jobs on `ubuntu-latest`. Run the
same commands locally before pushing:

* Server build + integration test:
+
[source,shell]
----
cd server
cmake --preset default
cmake --build build
python -m pip install -r ../tools/requirements.txt
python -m pytest ../tools/test_movement_milestone.py -v
----
* Python tooling lint:
+
[source,shell]
----
ruff check tools/
----
* Godot headless project validation:
+
[source,shell]
----
godot --headless --path client --quit
----

== C++ hygiene

Server code uses C++20.

Prefer:

* RAII
* explicit ownership
* value semantics where appropriate
* strong types
* composition
* small focused modules
* deterministic behavior
* standard library facilities

Avoid unless clearly justified:

* raw owning pointers
* global mutable state
* macro-heavy designs
* deep inheritance trees
* unnecessary template metaprogramming
* hidden side effects
* premature optimization

== Python hygiene

Maintained Python tooling should use:

* `ruff`
* `pytest`
* type annotations for non-trivial public APIs where practical

Tools must return non-zero on validation failure.

Avoid unnecessary dependencies.

== Godot hygiene

The Godot client is primarily presentation and input.

Do not move authoritative gameplay rules into the client.

Keep scripts and scenes small and purpose-specific.

Headless project validation must remain green.

== Test hygiene

* New behavior requires tests at the lowest useful level.
* Bugs should receive regression tests where practical.
* Do not delete, skip, weaken, or broaden test tolerances merely to make CI green.
* Tests must not depend on external internet services.
* Prefer fake time, explicit ticks, or synchronization over wall-clock sleeps.
* Integration tests should exercise real process boundaries where useful.
* Tests should be deterministic.

== Documentation hygiene

* Technical documentation under `docs/` uses AsciiDoc.
* Technical diagrams use PlantUML source.
* Documentation changes belong in the same PR as the implementation they describe.
* Stale diagrams are defects.
* Significant decisions receive ADRs.

== Dependency hygiene

* Add dependencies only for a clear need.
* Prefer mature and maintained libraries.
* Control versions sufficiently for reproducible CI.
* Verify licenses before merge.
* Document significant dependencies and why they exist.

== Security hygiene

Treat all network input as untrusted.

Validate:

* message sizes
* message types
* identifiers
* ranges
* state transitions

The server remains authoritative even if the client is modified or malicious.

== Change hygiene

* Keep PRs small and single-purpose.
* Avoid unrelated refactors inside feature PRs.
* Do not leave dead code.
* Do not leave commented-out implementation code.
* Deferred `TODO`/`FIXME` items should reference tracked work where appropriate.
* Do not silently change public interfaces or protocol behavior.

== AI-specific hygiene

Agents must:

. read `AGENTS.md`
. read the relevant docs before editing
. stay within issue scope
. update docs alongside relevant behavior changes
. run local validation before pushing
. preserve quality gates
. surface conflicts instead of guessing
. propose an ADR when a new foundational architectural decision is needed

Agents must not:

* invent architecture when documentation already defines it
* disable tests or linters to get green CI
* expand scope without approval
* add reuse rights or licenses without explicit instruction
